name: Federalism Templates
region: Global (Haudenosaunee territory, Switzerland, Netherlands, Nigeria, India, EU)
summary: Governance architectures that distribute sovereignty across nested levels — confederacies, federations, and cantonal systems — preserving local autonomy while enabling collective action.

claims.statement: The Haudenosaunee Confederacy (Great Law of Peace, c. 1142 CE) established a multi-nation federation with separated powers, bicameral deliberation, and subsidiary sovereignty that directly influenced American constitutional framers
Swiss cantonal federalism (1291–present) demonstrates that linguistic, religious, and cultural diversity can be governed without assimilation through radical subsidiary sovereignty
Post-colonial federalism in Nigeria and India adapted federal templates to manage ethnic and linguistic diversity at continental scale, with mixed but structurally resilient results

evidence.source: Parker (1916) The Constitution of the Five Nations (Iroquois Book of the Great Law), New York State Museum Bulletin 184
Grinde & Johansen (1991) Exemplar of Liberty: Native America and the Evolution of Democracy, American Indian Studies Center, UCLA
Linder (1994) Swiss Democracy: Possible Solutions to Conflict in Multicultural Societies, Palgrave Macmillan
Stepan (1999) Federalism and Democracy: Beyond the U.S. Model, Journal of Democracy 10(4)
Adeney (2007) Federalism and Ethnic Conflict Regulation in India and Pakistan, Palgrave Macmillan
